solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Author in online catalogue after end of autumn

parts.note: November is the last month of autumn, abbreviated to its first three letters
an e-list is a list kept electronically

explanation.surface: A writer turns up in a web listing just as autumn draws to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of autumn' tempts you to take the letter N, but here it is the whole month: November closes the season, and NOV is its calendar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist is a writer of long fiction, one particular kind of writer.

clue.text: Stated opposition about very small service

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a spoken vote against is a 'nay'
V is the abbreviation for very, and a small letter is all it takes

explanation.surface: A spoken objection is raised about some tiny act of service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very small' reads as one phrase of size, but it means 'very' shrunk to its abbreviation V.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Navy is one of the armed services, the sea-going branch of the military.

clue.text: As such, there's no difference between best and worst

definitions.text: As such, there's no difference between best and worst

parts.words: there's no difference between best and worst
parts.note: surface reading: a paradox in which the top and the bottom come to the same thing
setter's reading: used as parts of speech, 'best' and 'worst' both mean to defeat someone, so in that grammatical role they are identical

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a cynical remark about quality, but 'best' and 'worst' can both be used with an object meaning 'beat': to best or to worst an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the grammatical class of action words, the role in which these two superlatives mean exactly the same thing.

clue.text: Learner with an unhappy experience, one who's invested in his fields

definitions.text: one who's invested in his fields

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
taken as written
a downer is a depressing experience

explanation.surface: A novice farmer has a miserable time after sinking money into his own fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' suggests money in shares, but it is money tied up in land. A downer is informal for something that depresses you.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who owns acres of property has put capital into that ground, so the owner is the investor.

clue.text: What causes communal tension? It's Americans out of order

indicators.note: things out of order are jumbled from their proper sequence, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, twelve letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone asks what stirs up trouble between groups and blames badly behaved Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a political jibe, with 'out of order' meaning misbehaving; cryptically it asks for the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry between religious or political factions is a classic source of strife between communities living side by side.

clue.text: Go quickly out of control, indication of indecision after caution

indicators.note: coming after places one piece behind the other in the finished word

parts.note: care is caution
'er' is the hesitant noise someone makes when unsure

explanation.surface: A driver hesitates after being warned, then goes hurtling off the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first here; ER is the standard crossword hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to rush headlong in an uncontrolled way, like a car swerving down a hill.

clue.text: Alternative to reveille in Territorial Army

indicators.note: something contained within a longer stretch of text sits inside it, waiting to be spotted

parts.note: the end of the first word runs straight into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Reservists in camp are woken by something other than the usual bugle.
explanation.walkthrough: The military setting makes 'Territorial Army' look like the TA, Britain's volunteer reserve force, but its letters are the fodder. The word comes from Italian 'all'arme', 'to arms'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both reveille and a wake-up bell rouse sleepers; one is the bugle call in barracks, the other the clock by the bed.

clue.text: Plays some music, say — record isn't a remix

parts.note: to enter data is to record it

indicators.note: a remix rearranges an existing track, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A DJ insists that the disc on the turntable is an original, not a remix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' is a disc in the surface but a verb in the wordplay, and 'remix' works on the three short words beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing music for an audience is one example of amusing people, hence the 'say' flagging an instance.

clue.text: Toughness on island in sound? Just the opposite

parts.note: RE means 'on the subject of', as in a letter heading

indicators.note: one thing placed within another ends up enclosed by it

parts.note: the opposite of sound is quiet, the absence of any noise
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone praises the hardiness of life on an island, then asks whether it is in fact quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' looks like it should flip the whole clue, but it only turns 'sound' into its antonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The ability to recover quickly from difficulty is a form of hardiness or strength of character.

clue.text: Saintly female in charge in place of a couple of gentlemen

indicators.note: whatever is in something else lies inside it, enclosed on both sides

parts.words: place of a couple of gentlemen
parts.note: Shakespeare's comedy The Two Gentlemen of Verona is set in that Italian city
IC is the abbreviation for 'in charge'

explanation.surface: A holy woman takes charge in the home of two gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'couple of gentlemen' are Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona. Saint Veronica is said to have wiped Christ's face on the way to Calvary.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a woman venerated as a saint in Christian tradition.

clue.text: Predator that apparently prays in mass with enemies

indicators.note: being with something puts it alongside, so the parts sit side by side

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics
antis are people opposed to something

explanation.surface: A hunter who seems to be praying attends Mass among its foes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a church service to go with praying, but it is just the physics symbol M.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is an insect hunter named for the way it holds its forelegs folded as if in worship.

clue.text: Hostile frenzied action gains time

indicators.note: something frenzied is wild and chaotic, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An aggressive, frantic move buys a team extra time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frenzied' applies to everything after it, including the T from 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone actively opposed or unfriendly towards another party.

clue.text: One of seven letters from country admitting old novelist and, separately, me

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is let inside another
separately means apart, so the two inserts go into different gaps rather than side by side

parts.note: country as an adjective, as in country life
O is the abbreviation for old
Thomas Mann, the German author of The Magic Mountain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A letter comes from a nation that takes in an elderly writer, and me too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is the adjective, not a nation. 'Separately' means the two inserts go into different gaps of the host rather than side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman counting system uses just seven symbols, I, V, X, L, C, D and M, each a capital letter.

clue.text: Impassive fire controller, female, provided great service

parts.note: a poker is the iron rod used to tend a fire
F is the abbreviation for female
in tennis, to serve an ace is to serve an unreturnable ball

explanation.surface: An unflappable woman in charge of fire safety is praised for her excellent work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' reads as work or duty, but it is the tennis serve; an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A card player hides emotion behind a blank expression, so the term means showing no feeling.

clue.text: Block proposal for cinematographic technique

parts.note: to block is to prevent
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: Someone vetoes a plan to use a particular way of shooting a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are plain synonyms, read in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Animators photograph models one frame at a time, moving them slightly between shots, to create apparent movement on film.

clue.text: About half of score in many cases

parts.note: 'of' can mean concerning, as in 'a tale of two cities'
a score is twenty, and half of that is the number spelt here

explanation.surface: Roughly half the points are scored in most instances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it means roughly, but it is 'of' in the sense of 'concerning'. A score is twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens frequently occurs on numerous occasions, so the adverb matches the phrase.

clue.text: Far from lively prisoner sheltering a new one

indicators.note: a shelter surrounds what it protects, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: an inmate is someone held in a prison
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dull, listless convict gives shelter to a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A new one' reads as a fresh arrival, but it breaks into three single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without life or movement is the extreme opposite of energetic and animated.

clue.text: One Parliamentarian with kind of voice that's influential

indicators.note: being with something puts it alongside, so the parts sit side by side

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a Member of Parliament
in grammar, the active voice contrasts with the passive

explanation.surface: A politician with a commanding way of speaking wields real sway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voice' suggests speech, but it is the grammatical voice of a verb, active or passive.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a strong effect on events or people is what having influence amounts to.

clue.text: Naturally nobody speaks this strangely neat prose

indicators.note: something done strangely is done oddly, so these letters come out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tidy piece of writing that nobody would naturally say out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naturally' belongs to the definition: the invented language has hardly any native speakers, it is learned rather than acquired.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an artificial international language devised in the 1880s, so almost no one grows up using it as a mother tongue.

clue.text: At home wearing headgear, having turned back flap

indicators.note: turning back means facing the opposite way, so the letters run right to left
whatever wears a garment sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cap is a hat
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Someone indoors in a hat turns back the brim of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' looks like a piece of the hat, but it is the informal noun for a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flap is British informal for a state of nervous alarm or fluster.

clue.text: Illustration in book is central to revised perfection

indicators.note: being central to something means sitting in its middle, surrounded on both sides
revising text changes and reorders it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A picture in a book is said to be the heart of a newly polished masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters are rearranged first, and the two-letter word then goes into the exact middle of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the decorative picture facing a book's title page, a specific kind of printed illustration.

clue.text: Gripping part of hobby

parts.note: surface reading: the most absorbing aspect of a pastime
setter's reading: a hobby is a small falcon, and the part it grips with is a bird of prey's claw

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping' seems to mean enthralling and 'hobby' a pastime, but the hobby is a small falcon found in Britain and 'gripping' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of prey seize and hold their victims with hooked claws on their feet.

clue.text: Parts of body more than twice as long as hands

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the extremities we stand on

definitions.text: more than twice as long as hands
definitions.meaning: second meaning: units of length of twelve inches, three times the four-inch hand used to measure horses

explanation.walkthrough: A hand is an old unit of four inches still used for the height of horses, so the twelve-inch unit is three hands long, comfortably more than twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the body parts at the ends of the legs and imperial units of twelve inches.

clue.text: Parrots, for example, sent up for bit of flight

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: parrots are commonly kept as household animals

explanation.surface: Parrots are launched into the air for a short spell of flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests birds, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase is made up of individual treads, each one a single stair within the run.

clue.text: Hot ingredient for sauce, despite what you hear

indicators.note: what you hear is the sound of a word rather than its spelling, so the letters come from pronunciation

parts.note: the spoken word for this fiery pod is identical to the adjective meaning cold, which is the contradiction 'despite' points to

explanation.surface: A cook adds a fiery spice to the sauce even though its name suggests something cold.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate fodder: the definition itself, spoken aloud, sounds like 'chilly', meaning cold, the opposite of hot. 'Despite' flags that contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The small red or green pepper pod adds fiery heat to cooking and is a staple of spicy sauces.

clue.text: Small missile making shrill noise

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Trident is the ballistic missile carried by British submarines

explanation.surface: A little rocket whistles loudly on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is the name of the nuclear missile system on Britain's submarines, as well as the three-pronged spear.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a loud, harsh, grating sound, the kind that sets teeth on edge.

clue.text: Having a meal, sound as a bell, content to be doubled up?

indicators.note: doubling up means a second copy is added, so the inner part appears twice within the same shell

parts.note: the ringing noise a bell makes
the content of that bell noise is its middle pair of letters

explanation.surface: Someone eating is fit and healthy, happy to be bent double.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound as a bell' means perfectly healthy in the surface, but here it is the noise itself. Its inner two letters are then repeated inside the outer two.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating dinner or any meal is what the present participle describes, as in 'we were out at a restaurant'.

clue.text: Kind of bottle sailors found in end

indicators.note: whatever is found in something lies inside it, enclosed on both sides

parts.note: to end is to stop
a crew is the sailors who man a ship

explanation.surface: Seafarers turn up inside a bottle, like a message in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine and soft drinks often come with a threaded cap that twists off instead of a cork.
